title: More than 300 bird species use the Danube Delta
body: The Danube fans out into lakes, marshes and channels before it reaches the Black Sea. UNESCO records more than 300 bird species in this European delta, where habitats include both open water and thick reed beds.
takeaway: A river mouth can provide several habitats in the same area as water spreads out and slows.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Danube Delta (1991)
visual: a low aerial view of reed beds and channels opening towards the Black Sea

title: The Wadden Sea exposes vast mudflats at low tide
body: The Wadden Sea World Heritage property covers about 11,400 square kilometres along the coasts of Denmark, Germany and the Netherlands. Much of the landscape alternates between shallow water and exposed sand or mud as the tide moves.
takeaway: For migrating shorebirds, the receding tide opens a feeding ground that disappears twice a day in many places.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Wadden Sea
visual: shallow channels winding across broad tidal flats beneath wheeling shorebirds

title: More than two-thirds of Earth's fresh water is frozen
body: The US Geological Survey estimates that ice caps, glaciers and permanent snow hold about 69% of all Earth's fresh water. Groundwater accounts for most of the rest, while lakes and rivers hold much smaller shares.
takeaway: Fresh water on a map tells you very little about how much of it is available at the surface.
source: US Geological Survey, Water Science School, Where Is Earth's Water?
